$comment: THE CONTRACT BETWEEN TWO REPOSITORY HALVES THAT NEVER IMPORT EACH OTHER.
The identity service advertises a dial address in GET /.well-known/memql-config.json
(component/identity/discovery.go). Clients read that field and turn it into a
connection -- editors/vscode/src/connection/endpoint.ts lifts it to a /memql/ws URL.
Nothing in the build links the two, so for the whole life of memql#3399 the cluster
advertised 'https://bff.local.znas.io': a URL form the parser refuses outright, at a
host with no ingress. Both halves were individually tested and green.
This file is the single statement both halves are tested against. 'advertised' is what
the identity handler must emit for the given configuration; 'webSocketUrl' is what the
extension's parser must derive from it. 'rejected' lists spellings the document must
NEVER publish -- the TS side proves the parser refuses them, the Go side proves the

cases.name: the deployed local value: the cockpit front door, explicit 443
the deployed cloud value: base's placeholder front door, patched per overlay
memql#3399 regression: a scheme-ful operator value is normalized, never republished as a URL
scheme plus an explicit non-default port keeps the port
a plaintext scheme survives as a plaintext dial address
a trailing path is not part of a dial address
a bare host gets the front door's port
a bare loopback host gets the plaintext dev port
no override, TLS identity origin: the identity host at 443
no override, loopback dev origin: the HTTP port is NOT the gRPC port
an unusable override falls back to the derived default rather than publishing garbage
